findings.passage: Since 2018, I have been deeply involved in the Gun Violence Prevention movement–and now, as a State Representative, I am proud to have introduced legislation to recognize this day as Gun Violence Awareness Day in Wisconsin,
findings.note: Press release from her office for Gun Violence Awareness Day. She describes her involvement in the gun violence prevention movement since 2018 and her resolution.

findings.passage: We must take steps to prevent gun violence now. Firearms are the leading cause of death for children and teens in the United States, and second in Wisconsin.
findings.note: Same release. She calls for action and cites statistics on gun deaths. The release also says the 'Safe Summer' package she joined would require universal background checks on all gun sales, set a 48-hour waiting period, create Extreme Risk Protection Orders and ban ghost guns.

findings.passage: Time and time again, the research shows that prevention measures reduce gun violence and improve public safety.
findings.note: Same release. She says research supports prevention measures.
Her press release says she introduced Assembly Joint Resolution 61 on May 16 to mark Gun Violence Awareness Day in Wisconsin.

findings.passage: The people of Wisconsin want us to reduce gun violence. This does the opposite.
findings.note: Quoted by the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel (read on Yahoo News) in an article on a rally for gun safety laws and on competing bills, including bills on permitless carry.
